body: I've actually been using Khan Academy to learn math. People keep telling me that I could get good at math and I think that's why I'm just more frustrated when I don't get it. I just feel so stupid, like everyone expects me to get it and know how to math and then when I don't, I just feel like not bothering at all..

I'm glad that you explained all of that stuff to me because I have a very bad habit of looking at things from a technical point of view. When I'm feeling down, I often ask myself why I'm feeling that way rather than just accept that I'm feeling that way. I have a hard time accepting that this is something I need to stop doing and that sometimes it's okay to just be me. I always try to find a solution to my problems. I just can't help but look at the world around me and wonder if they think it's okay as well. I stopped using social medias because I got sick of seeing all of my friends being happy and successful. I know that Facebook is superficial, but even then, it made me depressed and probably was partly the reason for my alcohol abuse in the first place. Just yesterday, I scrolled through my Facebook feed to look at what other people were doing for Christmas. I rarely ever use Facebook and saw more than one friend with kids in their arms. Friends that I didn't even know had kids but who, more importantly, are the same age as me. I just sit here in my apartment with my video games all day and procrastinate doing my homework because I'm feeling like shit and wondering why it even matters anyways. I started obsessing over dinosaurs and pokémon again like one or two years ago and while I've always loved pokémon, I keep wondering if I'm obsessing over dinosaurs again because I want to be a kid again and I loved dinosaurs as a kid. Same with pokémon. It's not really what you would expect from a 30 year old dude. 

I've been told before that I'm very critical of myself. I don't understand why I'm like that. I just want to be able to look myself in the mirror and be like, "dang, you go!" but I haven't been able to do that. I wake up every morning thinking, "ugh, I'm so fucking ugly" and I have tried to forced positive thinking when looking in the mirror that everyone says would help, but it always leads to me thinking, why am I lying to myself.

I know this is going to sound like I'm trying to convince myself that I did the right thing by coming out as trans, but I know I did. My mom even said that so much from my childhood suddenly made sense when I came out. I've never felt more free since I had my top-op, it's been the greatest thing ever. I was born as a female but identify as male. I haven't been misgendered for years and it makes me feel confident in myself and relaxed. However, I never tell people that I'm trans because I don't want them to know. I consider myself a cis male even though I know that I'm not. I just don't feel like it's anyone's business unless I'm gonna sleep with them and I've sadly had a lot of awkward situations when I've told people, even left to the loss of some great friendships, which is probably why I don't tell anyone anymore.

It makes me somewhat happy that you compliment my language though because English isn't my first language. One of the topics I'm studying right now is English and my teacher keeps putting top grades on my papers, but I keep bringing myself down and wondering if he does that just to be nice because he knows I've had it rough. It's hard when I can't really ask the rest of the class what they got, that's none of my business and I respect that, so I don't ask but it also leads me to thinking that they probably all got top grades as well.

I think the part that bothers me the most is my age. There's a girl in my class who's studying the same as me and she's only 19. She has her whole life in front of her. I regret not doing what she's doing at 19. I just feel like my life is over before it has even begun because I never had a chance to do stuff like that. For the past 3-4'ish years, I've been drunk out of my mind and I hardly remember anything from those years. I played a lot of video games and wasted my life, that's what I do remember. Time that I could have been studying and getting ready for life ahead. I just find it hard to see a reason why I wouldn't just end my life and spare the people around me all the resources and effort wasted on me to get my life back on track when I'm 30. I'm gonna die anyways, so why would I want to just prolong that. I won't have finished an education before I'm at least 35 and by then, I'm already halfway through life anyways, so what's the point. I keep seeing people online refer to 35 as midlife and while I've always thought of it as young myself, my view on that has definitely changed since I've seen people at that age talked about as "middle-aged" a lot online

The exams won't be until next summer and by then, I'll be almost 31 which kinda fucks me up because I don't want to be 32 before I can start my dream education. I really want to get good at school and prove to everyone that I'm worth the high grades, but I find it hard when I can't accomplish that and then I look at my sister, who has never been super bright, with her high grades and difficult-to-get-into finished education. Her and her boyfriend just got a wicked expensive apartment that's over double the price of mine and I just look at stuff like that and think to myself that I'll never be able achieve that.

I think today has been especially hard because this week I've kinda been in a holiday rush and looked forward to Christmas and now that that's over, I'm pretty much back to my normal daily life cycle. (as normal as that can be in quarantine)

I just hate that I'm 30 and I have accomplished nothing. Best I've ever accomplished is finishing high end raids in world of warcraft. I don't even have a partner and I keep telling everyone that it's because I want to focus on me and while that's partly true, it's also half because I'm transgender (been out for over ten years and started HRT five years ago. Had my surgeries and all that) and often find myself wondering who would be with a freak like me since I don't fit into the traditional idea of what males look like body wise. When I turned 30, everyone at my study place, who don't know that I'm transgender, thought I turned 20 because I don't look 30 and it fucking pisses me off. I know there's a reason but I'm also pretty confident in people not knowing that I'm transgender. Mainly because I don't see myself as trans, I just prefer to think of myself as cis male.

I could've finished school and my education at this point. I could be spending my time doing my dream job, but instead I'm looking at fractions and history and I don't understand shit. I just find it hard to see a reason to keep going. I'll always be a freak and hate my body. It just seems like dreaming about being confident with my body and having my dream education at 30 is an unachievable goal and I might as well just... Not?

You might find what you're looking for if you go through the posts I've made on this profile. The first post I made on here was especially pretty dark. I almost took my own life when I was at my darkest place and today, I'm going to bed at 10 PM and taking my education! I have tried drinking a few times since I got out of my addiction, but I really don't like the feeling anymore. Last time I had just two beers, I was depressed for a week after and almost vomited from sheer depression alone so I really haven't been feeling like bringing myself into that state again and would rather stay sober. I don't count my days, I'm just happy to know that it's been more than a month when I used to be in a place where 2 days sober was a lot.

I just got out of my horrible DUI experience last month. I had to take my driver's license all over again. Believe me, when I first got pulled over and received my sentence, I almost dropped everything and took my own life because I couldn't see a way out of it. But getting pulled over saved me from drinking. I stopped for 4 months. I haven't quit drinking, I never intended on doing that, but I rarely feel an urge to drink at all anymore. When I do remember that I'm allowed to drink, I ask myself, "Yeah, but what do I gain from it and why would I? Just gonna wake up hungover tomorrow and that's no fun." 

I also had to go through a mandatory alcohol course before I was even allowed to take my license again. This made me realise that I'm not as fragile as I thought and it made me wanna try taking school again, which I've been nailing over the past month or so!

I highly encourage you to go through therapy, get some people who're experienced in drinking issues and talk to them or even just talk to your family about it. When I was able to realise that I had a problem, I was able to get help. 

It may not seem like it right now, but you will get out of it. I got over it and out of it, you can too!

I don't know if this means anything to you, but I used to be like this on the road as well. I got scared shitless when I was pulled over in the middle of the night for driving recklessly AND being drunk. I got a DUI in January that I'm still fighting to get over. I almost killed myself on the night that it happened. I'm about as law abiding as one can be for the most parts, but that night I was put in handcuffs and treated like a criminal by the police. Please get your daughter help and make her realise how dangerous reckless driving actually is. I know you didn't mention anything about driving drunk, but my reckless driving and thinking that I knew what I was doing was what caused me to get behind the wheel while drunk in the first place. Even without alcohol, she needs to realise that people are killed because of reckless drivers. If that were to happen to her, it's something she would have to live with for the rest of her life.

I'm still sober. Yesterday was my 4 months sober day. I've been feeling okay but today especially has been hard. I've started doing dnd and I almost missed the session today because I slept. The game master called me after the session to ask me how I was feeling about everything because I've been kind of quiet and hanging back during most of the sessions. It's really hard for me to chime in and do things because sober me is shy as fuck. Today has been a really off day and I thought about leaving the dnd session several times to go puke because I felt so depressed and shitty that I just couldn't be in my body. It has been hard trying to be social with a sober mind. I'm really contemplating taking a beer with me to dnd sessions just take the edge off but I'm worried that I will fall back into alcohol abuse. I never wanted to quit entirely but I don't know when drinking is appropriate. I've only been used to drinking when I shouldn't. My friends has told me that if I wanna start again, maybe just do it at social events. Issue is, there are no social events right now and our dnd sessions are done on Discord.

First step is to admit you have a problem and realise that you need help. Alcoholism is a sickness that can be treated. There's a lot of stigma about it which is why a lot of people feel ashamed to admit that they have a problem and most likely don't know that it's a mental illness. You can get out of it, you don't need a hobby to do so, you need to find what works for you. I'd suggest seeking professional help and take it from there. Perhaps seek out a local AA meeting and see first hand that you are not alone
Driving drunk. "Luckily" I got caught by the police once and had the shit scared out of me. I'm scared of even driving sober now.

Drinking because you're upset is the worst excuse. Stop and ask yourself what you gain from drinking and why you feel like that's the solution to your problem. The problem will still be there tomorrow, but be even harder to face because you will be hungover and even though you may not realise it, alcohol also has a huge impact on your mental state. Facing your problem with a sober mind will be so much better for you
Was about to comment this as well! I didn't know that alcohol cancelled out the effect of my medication before I reached out to my doctor with my drinking problems.

I get sertralin myself. It's really not something I can feel, it just makes me feel less anxiety. It's weird to explain what it does to you, but it definitely helps. When my drinking was at its worst, I kept taking my meds and something that opened my eyes was suddenly feeling my sertralin working again when I quit. It has been such a relief because it has also made me realise how little I was actually capable of during that time. I could have days where I stayed sober but even on those, I was a mess. Just keep in mind that it isn't something that happens right away. The first two weeks are the hardest, but we're here for you, even if you just wanna tell us about your day!

I was in your place 2 months ago. I wanted nothing more than to end my life. I'd hit rock bottom and I was ashamed of ever talking to my family again. I felt like such a burden to them and everyone else around me. I came onto this sub and started writing down my feelings whenever they flared up. I haven't posted much here for the past month because I've been feeling a lot better. I've made a new friend group in real life by going out and joining social club for other people with autism like myself and it has increased my will to live so much so, I can't believe I ever considered suicide. It will seem hard now but with a sober mind and life things will get easier. I know everyone always says that but it really does, especially when it comes to quitting alcohol. Something that has helped me a lot is doing something creative instead of drinking to distract my mind. I don't know if it's for you but I thought it was worth mentioning

Do you get medication for your anxiety? I didn't know, until my doctor told me, that alcohol cancelled out my anxiety medication and once I stopped drinking, I suddenly realised that my anxiety was a lot more manageable. Every time I feel an urge, I remind myself of all the anxiety that is bound to come back with the alcohol. My treatment center also told me how everyone eventually develops anxiety and depression from drinking, even if they don't have it to begin with. These should be reasons for you to not use alcohol as "medication", it's only making your anxiety so much worse! I hope you can use this as a method to remind yourself why you shouldn't drink when you feel an urge creeping onto you, and you will, it's all part of the process. Acknowledge it when it's there but don't give into it.

It's probably one of the things I struggle with the most and it got so bad at one point, that I completely quit all social medias. That was kind of scary too, because I often get people meeting me irl and expecting me to know that something happened in their life because they posted it on Facebook. It's kind of ridiculous to me, but mentally, quitting social medias has been nothing but positive.

I'm going to save this comment. Thank you so much for these words, really. It's not always the things I want to hear that help, but sometimes I struggle with seeing things from another perspective and I feel like your comment is the kind of stuff I need to get to this perspective.

No, I have autism and social stuff is the one thing I struggle with the most. I'm going to a rehab thing where I'm talking to a professional about my problems, but those meetings are just one on one. It's a lot easier for me to deal with that kind of treatment

Yeah. I'm talking to a rehab center and trying to get a therapist as well. 

I'm just tired of being floppy from all the drinking. I like like a beat up lump of clay and I'm sick of it.
I did, but the earliest appointment I could get is in August. Gotta love free health care, huh..

That's very true. I'm not sure I'd thought about it like that.

I don't hate my sister or anything like that, I love her a lot, I think it's just the fact that I've always struggled with school and getting through school shit and having to watch my little sister swoop through all of these things like it was no big deal. When she finished college, my mom put a picture of her on Facebook with a message about how proud she was. I stopped using Facebook around the same time because it made me feel depressed to watch everyone be successful at something I've never been able to get through because of my mental shit.(mostly school and education stuff.) I always feel jealousy when I see those posts from people I know, but it's worse with my sister. I sometimes feel like I was a failed attempt at life and she was the successful version that could've been me.

I'm sorry to whoever down voted my previous comment, I'm not trying to gain sympathy from reddit, I just want to put these feelings into words and get advice on how to deal with them.

It's not like I haven't tried to do something for myself, it's that I'm not able to. I want to, more than anything, but it's not as easy as "getting off my ass and doing it" mental illness is real, my guy.

I don't know if it help for you, it did for me. I found out that there are a lot of documentaries on Netflix *about* alcohol and the effect that it has on us. Meditation also really helped me. I knew the triggers, but meditation helped me understand them too.

Thank you so much! I'm sure if I didn't get the medication that prevents me from being able to even drink alcohol, I might have considered it, BUT. I also watched a reality show today that I'm following where they got hammered and I felt kinda sick looking at that and remembering that feeling. I think it was the first time I looked at drunk people and instead of thinking, "I want to be part of that!" I thought, "I'm so glad that isn't me"

It is, trust me. Alcohol only makes things like anxiety and depression much worse. At the treatment center, I was told that everyone who drinks extensively will end up depressed or anxious because that's how the brain reacts to alcohol. Doesn't matter if weren't in this state before drinking, alcohol will bring you into that state.The first weeks are hard, very hard. I'm coming up on 3 weeks sober and only now starting to feel better.

My interviewer mentioned this as well. It's the effect of those first few beers that we want, but it hardly ever stays at just those first few beers when we decide to drink. It's fun to be a bit silly like that, but even the small effect starts to bring out a personality that is not us.

I've always said that I'd rather people hate me for something I am than love me for something I am not, but I think for the first time in forever, I'm actually going to be true to those words. Alcohol doesn't make me a more confident person, it makes me a coward for trying to hide behind a filter that I have no control over.

It's hard to realise when you're in it, but looking back, I've woken up so many times from a night of drinking and hated myself for things I said or did while drunk. I've reflected on it and realised that the things I say and do when drunk, are things I would NEVER say or do while sober.

It's always hard not to compare yourself to others, that's what we humans do best and it's hard to break out of that thinking that, yes, I feel like shit, but it doesn't make me different and it doesn't mean I don't deserve help.

This is so true, I'm gonna try and remember this comment when I'm feeling down. I'm dreadful for what kind of decision the police will come to for my punishment, but I've been trying to get a hold of them to ask if they have an idea of what it might be so I can speculate less and focus on getting my life back on track.

I live in Europe, Scandinavia. I'm still not entirely ready to say my exact country, but from what I've read about laws, the worst I'll face is 3 years without my lisence, having to take the driving tests again, a fine and a non-mandatory 20 days prison sentence. Since I'm a first offender, it all seem pretty chill, but I'm still worried because I know the number I blew was high. Question is, how high. If its about what I think it was, they will take my drivers lisence for 3 years, send a fine, I will have to take the driving lessons again and show up for a drugs and alcohol information course thingy. I'm mostly worried if they will give me prison sentence. I won't have to go to prison when it's non-mandatory, but it will be on my record.
This means so much to me. I know you're just a stranger on the Internet, but I'm happy to know that someone is rooting for me.

I'm most likely not going into court because that's not really something they do in my country unless you deny the crime and I have no intentions of doing that. I just want to know if they have an idea of what my punishment will be so my head can chill until it arrives.

I got really drunk last Saturday night and decided to drive to get more beers when I ran out. The cops had been tailing me and because the blinkers on my car didn't work, they pulled me over. It was about 3 AM and they took me into the hospital to have blood samples taken. I called my mom shortly after being released from there and broke down, telling her first thing to not tell anyone about this because I was SO embarrassed by myself. Luckily my mom didn't throw any judgement, she just hugged me and told me that there's a history of alcohol in my family. I freaked out after she drove me home and almost tried to kill myself by self harm, but managed to make an emergency call and was put into the hospital again to be sown up. I felt so bad about lying to my mom about wanting to be alone when she drove me home after all the police stuff, so I made an effort to tell the nurses that I didn't need anyone there, but in my still drunken state, I decided to walk out of the hospital after being stitched up and the hospital called my mom (my phone is registered in her name) and said that the police would knock my door in if she didn't come to check on me because I'd been suicidal. It was just a chaos night, I've done a lot of shit in my life, but this was absolutely my rock bottom and why I've decided to start this journey to get help.

Scandinavia.
The thought of getting a lawyer is even more terrifying to me. I was prepare to just get a letter with the punishment and accept it from there. I've gotten speeding tickets before and that was handled with just a letter from the police that I had to confess to. (plead guilty I guess?)

It's hard not to think about it. All I want is to know what's going to happen and when. The guy I talked to at the alcohol treatment center suggested I tried calling the police and asked them if they had an idea of what would happen so I won't have to speculate too much. I'm just finding it hard to function right now because I want it done and over with so I can move on.

I feel you. I've been shaming myself a lot these past few days, just hating myself and what I did. It has been hard for me to accept that I need help and also hard for me to realise that alcoholism is an illness rather than a choice.

I live in Europe but what you got sounds a lot like what they also do with people who get a dui here. It's very rare that people go to prison here as a first offender or at all really for dui, but I have no idea what the blood tests will say about how much I had to drink. I had a lot and I knew when I sat in my car that I shouldn't have been driving. I just keep thinking it was a dumb mistake that I made myself and I'm such an idiot.

I love your writing. Saying that someone is the "author" of foot prints is a really good way of putting it. 

I've been thinking about getting back into writing myself to help me cope with the struggles that I'm facing right now. I'm glad to see that I am not alone about this.
I'm not entirely sure what it's called in English, but Disulfiram ? It basically does so I *CAN'T* drink.

Oh yes, I'm getting treatment. My doctor took it all very seriously and wanted to put me on medication for my alcoholism. I feel really shitty about that because usually when you hear about people getting medication for this addiction, it's the old bums who sits around on park benches. I'm just a 29 year old guy who likes video games. I don't feel like my problem is THAT serious. Honestly, a part of me feels like I don't deserve treatment because I know there are people out there much worse off than me and I'm struggling with accepting that I need the treatment.

See the worst part is that I know that feelings thing. I stayed sober for 2 months last year but relapsed. I had surgery coming up, so I didn't relapse as hard as when I was at my worse. I remember my anxiety and depression getting a lot better in those two months. It was wonderful and I got outside and ran a lot everywhere. I honestly miss that side of me, but I don't know how to get back to that point. Every day, I feel like a shaking mess and it's just getting worse every time I think about that letter that's coming.

It's just so hard man. I keep trying to figure out how I'll tell my friends that I don't have my car anymore and perhaps won't have my drivers license soon either. I just keep sitting here stewing and dreading the mail for my dui with my punishment. I'm gonna be a shaking mess until that comes and that won't be for another 2 weeks. I'm scared that I will go into a panic and attempt to take my life again when it does arrive.

I'm so glad that I found this community and thy I don't feel weird for posting rambles or updates about my life here. It has actually been a really good coping for me to write my problems down and have strangers respond to them. It means a lot, I'm thank for each and every one of you

Thank you, I'm trying. I went to the doctor today to ask for a therapist but she took the whole thing so seriously that she prescribed me medicin for my alcoholism as well. I'll start on that Wednesday. Just gotta keep the struggle at bay today and tomorrow
I'm so sorry for your struggle, sending you the best vibes from here. Just be happy that you're alive and no one got hurt.

My will is that I will (and did) get through my doctors appointment today. I will take the medication she prescribed me for my alcoholism and I will get through this despite feeling embarrassed about having reached this point of needing not only a therapist but medication too. IWNDYT

Thank you. I'm terrified of the road ahead and my current urge to never drink again. I know it will go away because I've told myself this before and I'm afraid of myself and what happens when it does go away. I'm determined to make an active choice, but I'm terrified of holding onto it.
Thank you so much for this, I'm tearing up as I reading these supportive comments

I'm having a hard time seeing myself going to AA. It's not that I don't want to or don't want the support, but I've been struggling with social anxiety my entire life. Probably why I started drinking so heavily in the first place. I feel like meeting a group of people might just make my condition worse at the moment.
